claims.text: Single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit a non-monotonic thermal-conductivity response as chemical short-range order develops.
Crossing the SRO-cluster percolation threshold enhances phonon transport by creating coherent, low-scattering pathways.
HfNbTaTiZr is an example of a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy under the proposed conditions.
The initial alloy can be prepared as a random solid solution with negligible SRO.
Intermediate-temperature annealing nucleates and grows SRO clusters until they percolate across a grain.
The alloy remains single-phase bcc in the stated high-temperature operating regime.
Accurate prediction of SRO evolution requires an interatomic potential that captures the relevant attractive and repulsive chemical interactions.
Standard interatomic potentials may predict the wrong SRO evolution.
A connected SRO network reduces lattice distortion or modifies phonon dispersion relative to isolated SRO clusters.
Isolated SRO clusters act as phonon-scattering centers and reduce thermal conductivity, as purportedly observed in fcc systems.
Ordered SRO domains can have a substantially longer phonon mean free path than the disordered matrix because they have less mass-fluctuation scattering.
A percolating ordered network allows phonons to bypass strongly scattering disordered regions.
Thermal conductivity initially decreases as non-percolating SRO forms.
Thermal conductivity exhibits a sharp increase or inflection when SRO clusters percolate.
After percolation, thermal conductivity is higher than that of the random solid solution or the non-percolated SRO state.
The proposed enhancement does not apply if SRO causes phase separation rather than coherent ordered domains within a single bcc phase.
The magnitude of the conductivity change depends on the chemical interactions and phonon-scattering contrast between ordered and disordered regions.
APT and high-resolution STEM can quantify SRO-cluster size distributions, volume fractions, and the onset of connectivity.
The 3-omega method or TDTR can measure thermal conductivity across the proposed annealing and percolation series.
Inelastic neutron scattering or Raman spectroscopy can determine the phonon mean free path in these samples.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits a final conductivity that is merely higher than the non-percolated state while remaining below the random-state baseline, but the falsification rule rejects any conductivity at the threshold that is below the random-state baseline.

The hypothesis itself predicts an initial monotonic decrease before percolation, whereas the falsification rule says monotonic decrease up to the point of percolation is sufficient to falsify it. A decisive rule should instead test for the predicted increase or slope change at or beyond independently identified percolation.
